A small release with one real fix, and the first one published from
`Uplift-Foundation/Claude-Buddy` — the canonical repository. `v0.1.0-beta` was cut
from a fork before the project moved here; this is where releases live from now on.

Still a beta. The Windows installer's wizard in particular has not yet been
through a human's hands, only automated checks.

## Fixed: clicking an orb could fail silently on macOS

If macOS had not granted Automation permission — or had **invalidated** a grant it
previously gave — clicking an orb did nothing at all, with no error anywhere.

That grant is tied to the app's code identity, so anything that changes it
invalidates the permission. Rebuilding the app, re-signing it, or switching between
a locally built copy and an installed release all count.

The symptom is deeply misleading. A denied click looks exactly like a click that
landed on a terminal which was already in front, so if you only have one terminal
window there is nothing to notice — until you click from **another desktop**, where
it looks like a Spaces bug rather than a permissions one. Made worse by System
Settings → Privacy & Security → **Automation** not listing an app whose consent was
invalidated, so the obvious place to look is empty.

Claude Buddy now reports this instead of failing quietly, naming the fix. If you
hit it:

```bash
tccutil reset AppleEvents io.github.wtvamp.claudebuddy
```

Then click an orb and approve the prompt.

The underlying focus logic was never broken — tmux pane selection, iTerm2 and
Terminal.app tab selection, and Spaces switching all worked correctly throughout.
Only the error reporting was missing.

## Which file do I want

| Platform | Download |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon (M1 and later) | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.1-beta-osx-arm64.dmg` |
| macOS, Intel | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.1-beta-osx-x64.dmg` |
| Windows 10/11, 64-bit | `ClaudeBuddy-0.1.1-beta-win-x64-setup.exe` |

The .NET runtime is bundled; nothing else is needed. `SHA256SUMS.txt` covers every
file — verify with `shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS.txt` on macOS or
`Get-FileHash <file> -Algorithm SHA256` on Windows.

## Upgrading from 0.1.0-beta

**macOS**: replace the app in Applications. The signing identity is unchanged, so
your Automation permission carries over and click-to-focus keeps working. Hooks are
already wired; you don't need to run the hook installer again.

**Windows**: run the new setup over the old one. It upgrades in place, closing a
running copy if needed, and leaves your hook configuration alone.

## Installing fresh

**macOS** — open the DMG, drag Claude Buddy to Applications, then double-click
**Install Claude Code Hooks.command**. Launch from Applications; nothing appears in
the Dock and no window opens, which is correct — look in the menu bar.

**Windows** — run the setup. Per-user, so no UAC prompt. Leave both checkboxes
ticked.

### The hook step is not optional

Claude Buddy learns about your sessions from a hook Claude Code runs. Until it is
in `~/.claude/settings.json`, the app starts and runs correctly and shows **nothing
at all**. The installers offer to wire it up; let them. Existing settings are backed
up first, and re-running repairs rather than duplicating.

Hooks are read once at session start, so **restart any open Claude Code sessions**.

## Known limitations

- **Windows installers are unsigned** — SmartScreen warns; choose **More info → Run
  anyway**. The macOS builds are signed and notarized, so they open normally.
- **The Windows wizard has only been verified automatically.** Silent install,
  file layout, shortcuts, hook wiring, hook execution and uninstall are all
  covered by CI on a real Windows runner, but nobody has watched the wizard run.
- **WSL + tmux together isn't covered.**
- A session killed with Ctrl+C at a permission prompt can leave its orb stuck on
  amber. Right-click → *Reset this session to idle* clears it.
